title: Legacy socket transport retirement and migration timeline
creator: Avery Park
description: PRD-level ticket to retire the legacy socket-based streaming transport used by older SDKs and mobile clients. This ticket defines the timeline, acceptance criteria, migration guidance for clients, server-side fallback windows, telemetry requirements, and cross-team responsibilities. Goal: give customers clear, low-friction migration path to the unified v2 streaming API while minimizing live site risk and preserving metrics continuity.
scope: Announce deprecation, publish migration guides, ship SDK adapters and opt-in compatibility shims, run canary and beta rollouts, enforce request-level deprecation headers, collect migration telemetry, coordinate final cutoff with enterprise customers and partners.
out_of_scope: Rewriting third-party partner SDKs, migrating non-Redwood-hosted clients, changes to model runtime behavior unrelated to transport, or broader protocol changes to message payload schema (those will be separate PRDs).
migration_strategy: Three-track approach: 1) Automated client updates: ship v2 SDKs with transparent adaptor that upgrades legacy socket usage to v2 streams where possible. 2) Compatibility shim: server-side compatibility layer that accepts legacy socket handshakes and converts them to v2 streams for a limited deprecation window. 3) Enterprise migration plan: account-level grace periods and a concierge migration program for large customers.
rollout_plan: Phase A - Announcement & docs (0-30 days): Deprecation notice, migration guide, sample code, and telemetry spec. Phase B - SDK releases (30-90 days): Publish v2 SDKs and adaptor with integration tests. Phase C - Canary (90-150 days): Enable compatibility shim for 10% of traffic, monitor errors and latency. Phase D - Opt-in enforcement (150-300 days): Emit deprecation header and start blocking new socket registrations without migration token. Phase E - Cutoff (>=300 days): Disable compatibility shim for general availability; provide final enterprise extensions by request.
timeline: Announcement: 2025-11-10. SDK beta release: 2026-01-15. Canary rollout start: 2026-04-01. Opt-in enforcement window begins: 2026-06-01. Compatibility shim scheduled removal: 2026-11-01. Final cutoff and sunset declared: 2026-12-01.
acceptance_criteria: Deprecation announcement published on status page, docs, and in-console banner
Migration guide with code samples for JavaScript, Python, Go, and iOS/Android published and reviewed by DX
v2 SDKs with adaptor packaged and passing integration tests in CI
Compatibility shim deployed behind feature flag and proven at 10% canary with <0.5% error delta vs baseline
Telemetry surfaced in Console: counts of legacy socket sessions, successful auto-upgrades, failed migrations, and customer opt-outs
Enterprise migration playbook created and trained with Solutions Engineering
Security review complete and KMS/HSM usage unaffected by shim
Customer support runbook and canned responses ready for public support teams
migration_guidance: Provide step-by-step samples: 1) Upgrade to latest SDK and enable adaptor flag. 2) Run test harness against staging environment using 'legacy-compat' header. 3) Validate token exchange and streaming frames with our provided trace tool. 4) If low-level socket semantics are used (resume tokens, client keepalive), follow advanced appendix. Encourage feature-flag toggles for gradual rollout. For mobile clients, recommend staged releases and telemetry gating to avoid mass churn.
risks: Large customers with proprietary socket implementations may require engineering time beyond standard SLA
Compatibility shim could mask client regressions and extend technical debt if left enabled past cutover
Telemetry gaps could undercount active legacy traffic, causing an earlier-than-safe cutoff
Mobile app stores timelines may delay client updates and require extended enterprise windows
